# Pending closes must preserve executable ownership

<a id="body"></a>

## Body

An acknowledged pending close must belong to a task that can execute it.
In #245, a new parent's close joined the old parent's pending task; the
original authority check correctly refused, silently losing the acknowledged
new close. A revived target caused the analogous failure.

Coalesce only the same close action, closer, process identity and pane.
Refuse mismatches explicitly with the pending deadline; never swap actors or
weaken the held task's authority/incarnation brakes. Check pending state
before note shortcuts and again at admission. Keep task-owned cleanup on
every closed/skipped/failed outcome.

Test composed transitions: reparent then repeat close, revive then repeat
close, and note-writing while close/compact is pending. Assert the typed
answer and prove a fresh close lands after the old turn releases its guard.

Reference: #245, reviewed head
`d43be5c79bc58cfbec035a4ba7cbdd8ab24a2615`;
`crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs` and
`crates/daemon/tests/memory_turn_http.rs`.
